a.raw: mr beaver caught some fish and mrs beaver fried them
a.fixed: Mr. Beaver caught some fish, and Mrs. Beaver fried them.
a.why: Mr. Beaver and Mrs. Beaver are titles and names. A comma goes before and. Caught is an irregular past verb.

b.raw: edmund crossed the river on the ice and he walked up to the house
b.fixed: Edmund crossed the river on the ice, and he walked up to the house.
b.why: Edmund is a name. A comma goes before and, because it joins two complete thoughts. Crossed and walked are regular past verbs.

cards.title: World Notes: The Full Moon
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: The moon does not make its own light. It shines with light from the sun.
Snow bounces light back, so a full moon on snow can make a night look almost bright.
In Chapter 9, the full moon comes out and helps Edmund find his way.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Look back at Chapters 7 to 9. Edmund and Lucy heard the same name and felt opposite things.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: roll not words, fix a passage in passes, and roll prefix words.
transcripts.guide2: Look back at Chapters 7 to 9 for your best details.

notes.wordParts: The word parts in- and im- both mean not. inactive = not active. impolite = not polite. Use im- before words that start with m or p.
notes.grammar: An irregular verb does not add -ed for the past. You learn each one: say → said, see → saw, sit → sat.
notes.spelling: A prefix goes on the front of a base word, and the base word keeps its spelling. Peel the prefix off to read the base: un + happy.
notes.wgrd: Lucy felt joy at Aslan's name and Edmund felt horror. What each one chose before changed what each one felt.
vocab: the right or power to give orders and make decisions
a statement that something will happen in the future
to be disloyal to someone who trusted you
betraying someone's trust in a very serious way

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Mrs. Beaver tells the children plainly that they cannot save Edmund by going to the Witch's House.
items.why: She tells them the hard truth to keep them safe.

items.t: Lucy reminds the others that Edmund was there when they talked about Aslan.
items.why: She tells what she remembers, even though it is bad news.

items.t: Edmund pretends to believe the Witch will not do anything very bad to the others.
items.why: Pretending to believe something is not being honest with yourself.
